{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — 18 rules assessed  
**Status:** 2 deviations requiring redline; 2 items flagged for review; 14 compliant

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The document is, on the whole, materially favourable to us: ownership of Customer Data and Deliverables, the licence grant, the Vendor indemnity (which sits outside the liability cap as an Excluded Claim), assignment and change-of-control, termination for convenience, transition assistance and data return, audit rights, insurance, governing law and renewal mechanics all meet our preferred position. The Agreement also imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-volume, MFN or non-solicitation obligation on us, and clause 12.3 affirmatively records the absence of those commitments.

Two issues require negotiation, and both sit in walk-away territory under the playbook:

- **Limitation of liability (§ 21).** The cap architecture (mutuality, carve-outs, indirect-damages exclusion) is sound, but "Fees" is defined in §§ 1.5/1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. The twelve-month look-back therefore captures no subscription or services charges, producing an illusory cap far below six months of actual fees and failing the fallback.
- **Liquidated damages (§ 7.7).** Customer-payable liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees for every week an invoice is late, triggered by a ten-day delay. This fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees), and the compounding weekly charge can exceed remaining contract value on a minor breach.

Two further items are flagged for review on verification grounds only, not because the substance is adverse to us: the non-solicitation finding (§ 12) and the performance warranty finding (§ 19). In both cases the substance sits at or above our preferred position; the failing checks are mechanical.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification | Preferred position met; indemnity obligations are Excluded Claims under § 21.3, so outside the cap. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables | Preferred position met in full; Deliverable ownership conditioned on payment of Fees and telemetry carve-out noted as customary. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability | Cap keyed to a "Fees" definition capturing only the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee; illusory cap, fails fallback. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control | Preferred position met; § 24.4 denies Vendor any repricing or termination right on our change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | No exclusivity on us; § 12.4 restraint runs in our favour and is not flagged. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes | § 7.7 imposes 15% of annual Fees per week of late payment after a ten-day delay; fails preferred and fallback. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence | Above the fallback; perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid rights extending to Affiliates and contractors. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binds us. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination | 30 days' notice under §§ 9.4 and 29.4; accrued Fees only, prepaid Fees refunded; Vendor has no convenience right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights | Preferred position met on every material term; § 22.3 adds Customer-favourable protections. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution | New York law and exclusive New York County jurisdiction; no arbitration provision. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes | § 7.6 runs in our favour; no MFN or price-matching obligation on us. Retain as drafted. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope | § 2.1: no minimum or purchase commitment; reinforced by §§ 7.1, 8.2, 8.3, 12.3. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | Preferred position met (no covenant binds us); two deterministic checks failed as phrasing tests with no covenant to narrow. Verification failed. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return | Six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; 30-day machine-readable return; deletion only after confirmed return. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, workers' comp; certificates and cancellation notice under § 18.2. |
| Low | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Needs review | § 19 Warranties | Substance at preferred position (90-day Deliverable warranty; Hosted Services for the subscription term). Period spelled in words only, which failed mechanical verification. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

Both items below are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature.

1. **§ 21 — Illusory liability cap.** Because "Fees" captures only the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, the twelve-month look-back yields a cap far below six months of actual fees. Our position: key the cap to all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor. The existing § 21.3 carve-outs, the § 21.2 mutual exclusion of indirect damages and the payment-obligations carve-out are acceptable and remain untouched.
2. **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** A 15% weekly charge triggered by a ten-day delay can compound past remaining contract value on a minor breach. Our position: delete the liquidated damages and substitute customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, preserving our § 7.3 withholding right. The playbook fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees) is available if Vendor will not accept deletion outright.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. **Issue redlines on the two deviations.** § 21 — replace the implementation-fee cap with the greater of twelve months of amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000. § 7.7 — delete the liquidated damages and substitute simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts. Both should be flagged to Vendor as gating.
2. **Confirm the "Fees" definition.** Any cap fix must be paired with a check of §§ 1.5/1.6 so the defined term does not continue to limit the cap basis to the Implementation Fee.
3. **Close out § 19 with a clarifying edit.** Insert the numeral so the period reads "ninety (90) days," with no change to the agreed period, scope or remedies. This resolves a verification issue that has twice caused the duration to be misread.
4. **Record the § 12 non-solicitation position as closed.** No covenant binds us and none should be introduced; we should not insert duration or general-solicitation language, as doing so would import a restriction adverse to us.
5. **Confirm no further redlines.** The remaining fourteen findings are compliant and require no changes; § 7.6 (Vendor MFN) and § 12.4 (Vendor competing-service restriction) run in our favour and should be preserved as drafted.

We are happy to circulate the two redlines for Vendor review once the deal team confirms the commercial fee figures behind the proposed cap basis."}
